text:
Olivia (customer): Hey team, hitting a weird issue with streaming responses. When we open an SSE stream for a long generation we sometimes get a 429 mid-stream and the connection closes. We've lost partial output and the client resumes by opening a fresh connection, which duplicates tokens/billing. Any ideas?

Maria (support): thanks for reporting, Olivia. Can you share a repro? curl or client code, timestamps, and the exact 429 body/headers would help. Also, which API key / org are you using (or a redacted one)?

Olivia (customer): repro below (sanitized). We open a streaming GET to /v1/streams with Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx. Sequence: first ~30s of stream ok, then server returns HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests and closes the socket. Body is a short JSON: {"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit"}}. Headers include x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and x-request-id. Our client code does: onclose -> attempt immediate reconnect with same prompt and resume logic that appends what we got. That ends up double counting ~150 tokens in billing.

Kevin (SRE): @Maria could you grab correlation id when this happens? Also, does the 429 happen only under concurrency (many clients) or single-stream? Any pattern with model choice / dedupe?

Olivia (customer): Single user session, concurrency 1. Model is open-variant-13b, long context. It happens more often when we have a long-running prefix and then user continues typing (so total token churn increases).

Maria (support): Ok. Two likely interactions: 1) quota/rate-limiter is counting per-request token budget once stream finishes; if the gateway enforces a per-second request rate or per-minute token cap and the stream was still consuming, the mid-stream limiter may fire. 2) auth key rotation or short TTL leading to an auth failure mid-stream (less likely with 429). Need logs.

DeployBot: New alert created: stream-429-spike (id: alert_2026_17598012). Notifying eng-runtime.

Kevin (SRE): I pulled logs for x-request-id from the sample header you pasted (redacted). The gateway rejected at the reverse-proxy layer due to token-bucket depletion: the per-key token bucket hit zero while the stream was active. The middleware treated the entire HTTP/1.1 connection as a request and didn't allow partial acceptance semantics for long-lived SSE. The proxy then returns 429 and terminates.

Evan (billing): Can you confirm the duplicate charge path? We're seeing usage rows where a partially-delivered stream then reconnects leads to two records: one with partial tokens and one with resumed tokens — we need to attribute to prevent customer-facing double-billing.

Maria (support): Olivia, to help us triage please try these repro steps so we get deterministic logs: 1) start an SSE stream with a small prompt that triggers ~400 tokens, use model open-variant-13b, request streaming with chunk interval 1s. 2) while streaming, send many short subsequent requests from the same key to force the bucket low (or run a load script that calls /embeddings concurrently). 3) capture response headers and the raw socket close event. Paste x-request-id and x-rate-limit-* headers.

Olivia (customer): I just ran that and uploaded logs to the share link (redacted). x-request-id: req-0a1b2c, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 14. Client saw: SSE "data: {\"delta\":...}\n" then a final HTTP/1.1 429. We also recorded socket close with ECONNRESET.

Kevin (SRE): Thanks. Looks like two interacting issues: the gateway's limiter is per-key across all endpoints and does not treat streaming token consumption atomically; and our billing pipeline currently records usage at request completions (and on reconnection we record the resumed request separately). That leads to the billing duplication you're seeing.

Maria (support): Short-term options for you: a) Reduce concurrent non-streaming calls while a long stream is active. b) Move to a Dedicated plan or raise the quota temporarily (we can bump your quota for 24h while you test). c) Use shorter streams with resumable offsets tracked client-side to avoid re-sending full prompt on reconnect.

Olivia (customer): Option b sounds useful for now. Can we increase quota quickly? Also, is there a server-side fix coming so 429 mid-stream isn't returned?

Evan (billing): We can apply a temporary quota increase for org redacted-org for 48h. I'll open a ticket and note it's for streaming stabilization.

Kevin (SRE): Long-term fix options being discussed by eng-runtime: 1) change the gateway to allow a streaming request to consume from a separate long-lived token bucket that charges continuously rather than by request completion; 2) emit a streaming-specific header with continuous usage so billing can be recorded as tokens are produced instead of at end; 3) implement a provisional 'stream-resume' token so clients can reconnect without recharging previous tokens. We'll need coordination across gateway, billing pipeline, and runtime.

Maria (support): I've escalated to eng-runtime and product. Internal ticket INF-3421 created with root-cause hypothesis and requested ETA. Pushed for a streaming usage header (X-Stream-Usage: tokens=NN) to be included in chunk footers as we generate them.

Kevin (SRE): Quick mitigation we can do sooner: adjust the limiter to treat in-flight streaming connections as exempt from per-second request rate when a separate per-token budget exists for that key. I can pilot this in staging and then prod-if-sane.

Olivia (customer): Appreciate the help. One more question: why did the client get a raw 429 body JSON instead of an SSE-friendly event so our client could resume gracefully?

Maria (support): Good point. Currently the proxy returns a standard HTTP error when it actively terminates a connection. We're tracking a change to emit a final SSE event `event: error\ndata: {"type":"rate_limit","message":"..."}\n\n` before closing so clients can handle it without ambiguous socket errors. Noted in INF-3421.

Evan (billing): Action items: apply 48h quota bump (ticket BILL-881). Follow-up once eng confirms a streaming usage header changes the billing dedupe logic.

Kevin (SRE): I'll run a staged limiter tweak and post results here. Maria — can you please set expectation with Olivia on timeline?

Maria (support): ETA: temporary quota bump applied within 2 hours. SRE will pilot limiter adjustment in staging within 24-48h. Engineering plan for stream-atomic accounting and SSE error events is under prioritization — target RFC in 1 week.

Olivia (customer): Thanks all. We'll test with the quota bump and let you know if reconnects still cause duplicates. Appreciate the quick response. :heart:

Maria (support): Closing loop — quota bump applied (Evan). Keep thread open for results. :thumbsup:

DeployBot: alert_2026_17598012 resolved (closed by Kevin).
